question: What are good high-energy toys and games to tire out my Labrador?
answer:
Tier 3 — my picks for a high-drive Lab (Common Sense Dog): Labs are bred to retrieve for hours, so they need real physical AND mental work or they get bored and destructive. What works: 

• AUTOMATIC BALL LAUNCHER / pitching machine (Furlihong brand on Amazon) — it launches balls so your Lab can fetch over and over and actually burn energy long after your arm gives out; great for a yard. Use the SOFT dog-safe balls it's made for — NOT hard baseballs (hard balls crack teeth). 
• FLIRT POLE (a 'fishing pole' style toy — a lure on a rope on a pole) — you swing it and the dog chases and pounces; burns a ton of prey-drive energy in short bursts even in a small space. Let them 'catch' it every so often so it stays rewarding. 
• WATER RETRIEVING — Labs are water dogs; tossing a floating bumper at a dog-safe lake or the ocean is ideal low-impact exercise for their joints. 

WHEN NOT to / safety (important): 
- AVOID GOLF BALLS entirely — they're a genuine hazard, not a toy: choking and gut-obstruction risk for big dogs, they crack teeth (fiberglass grinds enamel), and their cores contain toxic zinc compounds. Use a solid rubber ball sized so it can't be swallowed instead. 
- Skip hard baseballs (tooth fracture) — wiffle or soft rubber balls only, sized to your dog. 
- At the OCEAN: don't let your dog drink salt water (it causes 'beach diarrhea,' and in quantity, dangerous salt toxicity) — offer fresh water often, watch for rip currents and over-tiring, and rinse the salt and sand off the coat afterward to prevent skin irritation.
source: Kyle — Common Sense Dog recommendations (golf-ball hazard verified: choking/tooth fracture/toxic zinc core)
